skill.name: url-analysis
skill.description: Validate URLs, redirects, and contextual link quality in documents or single URLs using a Python helper and guided review.
skill.summary: Checks link health, redirects, and relevance for content review workflows.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: Most SKILL.md findings are false positives from Markdown code fences and example URLs. The helper does perform real outbound URL checks, and unrestricted user-controlled destinations create a moderate internal network probing risk.

remediation.suggestion: Block loopback, link-local, private, metadata service, and non-HTTP(S) targets before sending requests. Ask for confirmation before live network checks.
State that technical validation sends HEAD requests to each checked URL and may reveal that a link was checked.

remediation.issue: Helper script path is documented inconsistently
remediation.suggestion: Update the Markdown examples to use scripts/validate-urls.py so users run the included file.

semantic_findings.description: The helper accepts URLs from files or command line arguments and sends HEAD requests without private address, loopback, or metadata service filtering. A document with internal URLs could cause network probes from the agent environment.

content.value_statement: Broken, stale, or mismatched links reduce trust and waste review time. This skill checks link status, redirects, context fit, and quality signals for documents or single URLs.
actual_capabilities: Extracts HTTP and HTTPS links from provided text files.
Checks URL syntax before making a request.
Sends HEAD requests to measure accessibility and status codes.
Reports redirect targets and redirect chain length.
Guides contextual review of link text, relevance, source authority, and reader value.
limitations: Network validation contacts each checked URL and depends on remote server behavior.
The helper does not block private, loopback, or metadata service addresses.
SSL validity is inferred through the HTTP client, not reported as certificate metadata.
The documented helper path uses underscores, while the included file name uses hyphens.

use_cases.title: Documentation link review
use_cases.description: Technical writers can identify broken links, redirects, and link text mismatches before publishing.

use_cases.title: SEO quality audit
use_cases.description: Content marketers can find outdated destinations, weak landing pages, and redirects that affect search quality.

use_cases.title: Release checklist validation
use_cases.description: Developer advocates can check launch notes, examples, and reference links before a release.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Single Link
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this URL for syntax, accessibility, redirects, and likely context fit: [URL].

prompt_templates.title: Review a Document
prompt_templates.scenario: Find and validate links in a file
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract all URLs from [file or pasted content], validate them, and summarize broken links, redirects, and high priority fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Context Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate link text and destination relevance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the links in this article. Compare each link text with its destination purpose and flag mismatches or outdated sources.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Publication Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [document] for link health, redirects, HTTPS use, source authority, and reader value. Rank fixes by publication risk.

output_examples.input: Validate a blog draft with product documentation links.
output: The report identifies two redirects, one broken link, and one vague homepage destination.
It recommends updating redirect targets and replacing the broken reference.

output_examples.input: Check whether a tutorial link matches its anchor text.
output_examples.output: The link is reachable, but the destination is a homepage instead of a React patterns article. The report recommends a specific article URL.
The audit groups links by status, notes external domains, and ranks fixes by reader impact.

best_practices: Ask before running live network validation on private, sensitive, or unreleased documents.
Review redirects manually before updating important canonical URLs.
Pair technical status checks with human review of link relevance and authority.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a 200 status as proof that the destination is relevant.
Do not validate private intranet or localhost links without explicit permission.
Do not paste secrets into URLs or query strings for validation.

faq.question: Does this skill make network requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper sends HEAD requests to URLs being validated when technical checks are used.

faq.question: Can it validate URLs inside a document?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper extracts HTTP and HTTPS links from a text file and validates each one.

faq.question: Does it judge link relevance?
faq.answer: It can guide contextual analysis, but final relevance decisions need human review.

faq.question: Can it replace SEO tools?
faq.answer: No. It supports link quality review, but it does not crawl full sites or measure rankings.

faq.question: Does it verify SSL certificates?
faq.answer: The HTTP client verifies TLS during HTTPS requests, but the helper does not return certificate details.

faq.question: What should users check before running it?
faq.answer: Users should confirm that outbound requests are allowed and that the document does not contain sensitive internal URLs.
